title: When the Cipher Breaks
premise: When the coffin of town founder Aldous Wren is found empty during a routine exhumation, night-shift taxi dispatcher Bram Marchetti — an amateur sleuth whose three prior 'accident' cases were quietly solved from behind a radio console — is pulled in when the exhumation order traces back to an anonymous tip sent through the cab company's own dispatch line. Bram discovers the tip came from someone who knows the truth: thirty years ago, Wren faked his death to escape prosecution for a fire that killed four workers, and the town's founding families have been paying for his silence ever since. As the anniversary dinner approaches — the one night every heir, alibi, and lie gathers under one roof — Bram must decide whether justice means exposure or something quieter, and ends the book by letting the truth out not through the police but through the town itself, at the dinner table where the lie was first told.
about_author: Edmund Kavanagh is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper obituarist who spent a decade listening to what towns say about their dead — and what they refuse to. He writes mysteries about people who solve crimes because no one else will.

chapters.title: The Night Frequency
chapters.summary: Bram Marchetti's POV. A slow Tuesday shift at Kestrel Taxi dispatch; we learn how Bram reads a town through its ride requests, and how three 'accidents' were quietly unraveled from this chair. Emotional beat: competent loneliness, the comfort of patterns.

chapters.title: Dirt on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. News breaks: founder Aldous Wren's grave is being exhumed by court order after an anonymous tip. Bram recognizes the tip's wording — it was phrased like a cab call, routed through dispatch. Beat: unease; the pattern has found him.

chapters.title: What the Grave Gave Back
chapters.summary: Bram attends the exhumation crowd scene. The coffin is empty except for a brass plate engraved with a date thirty years past — the night of the Hollis Mill fire. Beat: public shock curdling into private fear among the old families.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Wren Trust insists the anniversary dinner will proceed as planned. Bram is hired — ostensibly — to arrange transport for elderly attendees, giving him legitimate access. Beat: wary opportunity.

chapters.title: Four Names in Ash
chapters.summary: Bram researches the Hollis Mill fire: four workers died, no one charged, Wren 'died' two years later of a heart condition. POV shifts briefly to retired coroner Ida Voss, who signed the death certificate and has never slept well since. Beat: guilt as motive.

chapters.title: The Tip That Called Collect
chapters.summary: Bram traces the anonymous tip through old dispatch logs to a payphone outside the defunct mill. Someone wanted him specifically. Beat: flattered and hunted at once.

chapters.title: Heirs and Apparents
chapters.summary: Introduction of the five founding-family heirs attending the dinner: Marianne Wren-Cole (granddaughter), banker Theo Ashcombe, councilwoman Ruth Delgado, recluse Peter Hollis Jr., and young journalist Sam Okafor. Bram's POV. Beat: a cast of locked-room suspects.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Vintage
chapters.summary: Ida Voss's POV. She recalls the night she certified Wren's death: the body she saw was real, but the name on it wasn't. She gives Bram her first crack in the wall. Beat: confession as relief.

chapters.title: Dead Man Driving
chapters.summary: Bram finds evidence Wren lived years after his death — a pension draft, a pharmacy record under an alias, all within twenty miles. Beat: the thrill of the hunt turning ominous when someone follows him home.

chapters.title: The Passenger Who Paid Cash
chapters.summary: A fare Bram drove months ago resurfaces in memory: an old man with burn-scarred hands who asked to be taken past the mill and said nothing else. Bram's POV. Beat: dread of recognition.

chapters.title: Ruth Delgado's Quiet Money
chapters.summary: Bram digs into trust disbursements: annual payments, disguised as grants, flowing from the Wren Trust to each family — hush money by another name. Beat: corruption revealed as infrastructure.

chapters.title: Sam Okafor's Deadline
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. The young journalist has been sitting on a source for months, terrified. She nearly tells Bram everything, then pulls back. Beat: cowardice and conscience wrestling.

chapters.title: Theo Ashcombe's Perfect Evening
chapters.summary: Bram checks Theo's thirty-year-old alibi — a gala photograph, time-stamped, ironclad. Too ironclad; the timestamp was corrected in the negative. Beat: the pleasure of finding the flaw.

chapters.title: Fire Weather
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ida Voss's POV, 1994: the night of the fire, the locked exit doors, the foreman's orders, and young Aldous Wren watching from the office window. Beat: horror without melodrama.

chapters.title: The Second Empty Grave
chapters.summary: Peter Hollis Sr.'s grave — the fire's foreman — is found disturbed. Someone got there first. Bram realizes he's racing another investigator. Beat: competition becomes threat.

chapters.title: Marianne's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Marianne Wren-Cole's POV. She knew nothing, she insists — but she's been receiving letters in her grandfather's handwriting, postmarked after his death. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Dispatch Log, Redacted
chapters.summary: Someone has accessed the cab company's archives; pages are missing. Bram's boss, Nell, admits she was paid to look away years ago. Beat: betrayal inside Bram's sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Man with Burned Hands
chapters.summary: Bram tracks the scarred passenger to a room above a laundromat: Elias Brandt, the fifth worker listed dead in the fire — alive, hiding, and the one who tipped the exhumation. Beat: the mystery's engine exposed.

chapters.title: What Elias Saw
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His account: Wren didn't die — he fled with the insurance money, and the families have sheltered him ever since, each taking a cut. But Elias wants more than truth; he wants the man himself. Beat: sympathy shading into menace.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: Bram receives a lawyer's letter and a subtler warning: his sister's lease, his mother's care home, both touched by Wren Trust money. Beat: power showing its teeth.

chapters.title: Nell's Confession
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Thirty years ago she was the dispatcher who drove the getaway car's second leg, believing she was helping a dying man reach hospice. Beat: complicity of ordinary kindness.

chapters.title: The Photograph Nobody Claims
chapters.summary: A recent photo surfaces: an old man resembling Wren at last year's anniversary dinner, seated at the edge, uninvited. One of the heirs let him in. Bram's POV. Beat: the walls closing in.

chapters.title: Which Heir Blinked
chapters.summary: Bram corners each heir separately. Ruth lies badly, Theo lies beautifully, Peter Jr. says nothing, Marianne cries, Sam finally shows him her source file. Beat: the net tightening around a single unknown protector.

chapters.title: The Protector
chapters.summary: Reveal: Ida Voss has been Wren's secret correspondent — not loyalty, but leverage; she kept him alive on paper so he could never fully vanish. Her POV. Beat: the coroner as jailer.

chapters.title: Where Wren Is Now
chapters.summary: triangulating pharmacy records, pension drafts, and one taxi fare: Wren lives in the converted mill itself, the crime scene turned hiding place. Bram's POV. Beat: dark poetry of the location.

chapters.title: An Offer from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Wren contacts Bram directly — calm, courteous, offering money and silence, and hinting he knows about Bram's three solved cases. Beat: seduction of power; Bram tempted for one long page.

chapters.title: What Bram Wants
chapters.summary: Quiet character chapter. Bram visits the fire victims' memorial wall, thinks about justice versus law, about belonging to a town that never noticed him. Beat: the theme made personal.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Depot
chapters.summary: The cab company's radios fail mysteriously on the eve of the dinner; someone wants Bram deaf on the crucial night. Elias is suspected. Beat: allies fracturing.

chapters.title: Elias's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Elias plans to take Wren at the dinner — publicly, violently if needed. He gives Bram until the toast to hand over the location or lose any claim to the moral high ground. Beat: ticking clock armed.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis, Cross-Checked
chapters.summary: Bram lays out the full board: who paid, who lied, who protected, who profited. He finds the one thread none of them know he has — the original dispatch log from the night Wren fled, in Nell's keeping. Beat: clarity before storm.

chapters.title: Invitations
chapters.summary: Bram does something unprecedented: he invites everyone — heirs, Ida, Elias, Nell, Sam — to the anniversary dinner, knowing Wren cannot resist attending the ritual built to honor his fake death. Beat: audacity.

chapters.title: Setting the Table
chapters.summary: Preparations, alliances, betrayals promised. Sam agrees to hold the story until midnight; Ida agrees to bring the death certificate; Nell brings the log. Bram's POV. Beat: fragile coalition.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The dinner begins. Toasts, evasions, Marianne reading her grandfather's letters aloud. Then the far door opens and an old man with burned hands walks in — but it isn't Elias. It's Wren himself. Beat: the trap springs both ways.

chapters.title: Confession at the Head Table
chapters.summary: Confrontation: Wren defends himself with chilling reasonableness — the town was built on his money, the fire was negligence not murder, everyone ate from his hand. Elias lunges; chaos. Beat: the climax's first break.

chapters.title: The Fire Rekindled
chapters.summary: In the struggle, a lamp ignites the old ballroom curtains. Smoke, stampede, Bram choosing between catching Wren and pulling Ruth Delgado from the flames. Beat: character defined by action.

chapters.title: Ashes and Answers
chapters.summary: Aftermath of the fire: Wren gone again in the confusion, Elias injured, the ballroom gutted. But Nell's dispatch log — smuggled out — proves the flight was premeditated, making Wren's death certificate fraud and the payments conspiracy. Beat: victory with ash in the mouth.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Bram chooses the town over the courts: he gives the full story to Sam Okafor and lets it print, rather than handing it to prosecutors entangled with the Trust. Arrests follow anyway; some flee. Beat: thematic resolution.

chapters.title: What Happened to Wren
chapters.summary: Weeks later, a final taxi fare: Bram drives an old man to the county line and lets him go, exchanging no words — justice served by exile, the only sentence Bram can impose. Beat: mercy as verdict.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name on the Wall
chapters.summary: The memorial wall gains a fifth name: Elias Brandt, restored to the dead of the fire even though he lives — his old life formally buried so he can begin again. Ida Voss retires, sleeping better. Beat: restitution.

chapters.title: Night Shift, New Frequency
chapters.summary: Bram back at the console, the town's calls flowing in, changed and unchanged. A new voice on the line asks for help with something that doesn't look like an accident. Beat: belonging found; the next case knocking.
